solutions.title: Install requests package in current active environment
solutions.steps:
1. Verify active python binary: `which python`
2. Install package via pip: `pip install requests`
3. Confirm installation: `python -c 'import requests; print(requests.__version__)'`

solutions.title: Explicitly invoke pip with python3 module flag
solutions.steps:
1. Determine interpreter path: `python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)'`
2. Run module install: `python3 -m pip install requests`
3. Execute script with matching interpreter: `python3 main.py`

solutions.title: Recreate corrupted Python virtual environment
solutions.steps:
1. Deactivate environment: `deactivate`
2. Remove corrupted directory: `rm -rf .venv`
3. Re-initialize venv: `python3 -m venv .venv`
4. Reinstall dependencies: `source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt`

title: Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3000

solutions.title: Identify PID using lsof and kill the lingering process
solutions.steps:
1. Find process holding port 3000: `lsof -i :3000`
2. Note the PID from the command output.
3. Terminate process gracefully: `kill -15 <PID>` (or `kill -9 <PID>` if unresponsive).

solutions.title: One-liner port killer using npx kill-port
solutions.steps:
1. Run npx kill-port utility directly: `npx kill-port 3000`
2. Re-launch dev server: `npm run dev`

solutions.title: Change PORT environment variable in .env file
solutions.steps:
1. Open `.env` or set variable inline: `PORT=3001`
2. Start server on secondary port: `PORT=3001 npm run dev`

title: npm ERR! code ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree

solutions.title: Install with --legacy-peer-deps flag
solutions.steps:
1. Run installation ignoring peer dependency mismatches: `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`
2. Test build output: `npm run build`

solutions.title: Delete node_modules and package-lock.json and rebuild
solutions.steps:
1. Remove lockfile and vendor files: `rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json`
2. Clean npm cache: `npm cache clean --force`
3. Run clean install: `npm install`

solutions.title: Use npm install --force override
solutions.steps:
1. Execute forceful dependency resolution: `npm install --force`
2. Verify peer dependencies for breakage.

title: Cannot connect to the Docker service at unix:///var/run/docker.sock

solutions.title: Start Docker systemd service
solutions.steps:
1. Start engine service: `sudo systemctl start docker`
2. Enable automatic start on boot: `sudo systemctl enable docker`
3. Check service status: `sudo systemctl status docker`

solutions.title: Add current user to docker group to fix socket permissions
solutions.steps:
1. Create group if not present: `sudo groupadd docker`
2. Append user to group: `sudo usermod -aG docker $USER`
3. Refresh shell session: `newgrp docker`
4. Verify without sudo: `docker ps`

solutions.title: Restart Docker Desktop application (macOS/Windows)
solutions.steps:
1. Quit Docker Desktop from the system tray / menu bar.
2. Wait 10 seconds for VM shutdown.
3. Relaunch Docker Desktop and verify whale icon stabilizes.

title: Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result

solutions.title: Resolve conflict markers manually and commit
solutions.steps:
1. Check conflicted files: `git status`
2. Open files and resolve `<<<<<<<`, `=======`, and `>>>>>>>` markers.
3. Stage resolved files: `git add <filename>`
4. Complete merge commit: `git commit -m 'Merge branch and resolve conflicts'`

solutions.title: Abort current merge safely to reset working tree
solutions.steps:
1. Abort the failed merge: `git merge --abort`
2. Ensure working directory is clean: `git status`

solutions.title: Checkout entire version from target or incoming branch
solutions.steps:
1. Prefer current branch: `git checkout --ours <filename>`
2. Or prefer incoming branch: `git checkout --theirs <filename>`
3. Stage and commit: `git add <filename> && git commit`

title: IBM Db2 SQL30082N Security processing failed / Connection authorization failure

solutions.title: Verify user credentials and instance container password
solutions.steps:
1. Confirm DB2USER matches instance user (typically `db2inst1`).
2. If using container, ensure container has finished initialization: `docker logs db2`
3. Reset password inside container: `docker exec -it db2 bash -c 'echo "db2inst1:new_password" | chpasswd'`

solutions.title: Verify Db2 communication protocol and port configuration
solutions.steps:
1. Inside Db2 container run: `su - db2inst1 -c 'db2set DB2COMM=TCPIP'`
2. Check listener port: `su - db2inst1 -c 'db2 get dbm cfg | grep -i svcename'`
3. Restart Db2 instance: `su - db2inst1 -c 'db2stop force && db2start'`

solutions.title: Check SSL/TLS connection parameter mismatch
solutions.steps:
1. Verify whether client specifies `SECURITY=SSL` when server uses plain TCP/IP.
2. For plain connections ensure `PROTOCOL=TCPIP` and port is `50000` (or `50001` for SSL).

title: CORS error: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present

solutions.title: Configure CORSMiddleware in FastAPI backend
solutions.steps:
1. Import middleware: `from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware`
2. Add middleware allowing client origin: `app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=['https://resolve-ai.vercel.app'], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=['*'], allow_headers=['*'])`
3. Restart backend server.

solutions.title: Configure VITE_API_URL environment variable for API endpoint routing
solutions.steps:
1. In `.env.local` set: `VITE_API_URL=https://resolve-ai-backend.railway.app`
2. In frontend fetch calls, read endpoint from `import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL`.

solutions.title: Add CORS headers in Express server
solutions.steps:
1. Install cors: `npm install cors`
2. In `server.ts`: `import cors from 'cors'; app.use(cors());`
3. Restart server.

title: Permission denied (publickey) when connecting via SSH

solutions.title: Add SSH private key to ssh-agent
solutions.steps:
1. Start agent in background: `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"`
2. Add private key: `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` (or `~/.ssh/id_rsa`)
3. Test GitHub connection: `ssh -T git@github.com`

solutions.title: Fix directory and key file permissions
solutions.steps:
1. Set .ssh directory permissions: `chmod 700 ~/.ssh`
2. Set private key permissions: `chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`
3. Set public key permissions: `chmod 644 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`
4. Re-test SSH connection.

solutions.title: Generate new modern Ed25519 SSH keypair
solutions.steps:
1. Generate key: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'your_email@example.com'`
2. Copy public key: `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`
3. Paste into GitHub/GitLab SSH keys settings.

title: Property 'X' does not exist on type 'Y' (TS2339)

solutions.title: Extend interface or type definition with optional property
solutions.steps:
1. Locate interface definition.
2. Add declared field with type: `property_name?: string;`
3. Re-run TypeScript compile check: `npx tsc --noEmit`

solutions.title: Use type guard or narrowing before accessing property
solutions.steps:
1. Check property existence with in operator: `if ('propertyName' in object) { ... }`
2. Or define custom type guard: `function isX(val: unknown): val is X { ... }`

solutions.title: Cast type using unknown intermediary (temporary fix)
solutions.steps:
1. Narrow via unknown: `(myVar as unknown as TargetType).propertyName`
2. Add TODO comment to refactor schema properly.

title: Hydration failed because the initial UI does not match what was rendered

solutions.title: Guard client-only state using useEffect and mounted flag
solutions.steps:
1. Create mounted state: `const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(false);`
2. Set mounted true in effect: `useEffect(() => setMounted(true), []);`
3. Render placeholder until mounted: `if (!mounted) return null;`
